newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index ends lower on caution.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index ends lower on caution.

text.p: Shenzhen's B shares ended slightly down on Tuesday despite a strong debut by Wafangdian Bearing 2706.SZ with investors taking quick profits amid uncertainty in the company reporting season, analysts said.
The B share index lost 0.86 points or 0.53 percent to 162.08 points. Turnover was HK$172.8 million compared with Tuesday's HK$76.8 million.
"Wafangdian's performance gave positive signals to the market, but investors are holding their breath ahead of the flood of annual reports expected very soon," a trader at J&A Securities said.
Only three out of the 44 B share companies listed in Shenzhen have made their results public, with the official April 30 deadline approaching.
Wafangdian, which debuted in Shenzhen on Tuesday, opened at HK$4.05 or 52.26 percent up on the issue price of HK$2.66.
It quickly hit an intraday high of HK$5.53 before profit-taking trimmed gains, traders said.
Wafangdian closed at HK$5.02, up HK$2.36 or 88.72 percent on its issue price as 18.6 million shares changed hands, making it the day's most active stock.
The market was also affected by Hefei Meiling Co Ltd which on Tuesday reported a profit surge in 1996 on strong demand for its refrigerators.
Meiling's 1996 net profit reached 138.34 million yuan compared with 95.1 million yuan in 1995 based on international accounting standards, company officials said.

But Meiling became the third biggest loser, dropping HK$0.17 or 2.71 percent to end the day at HK$6.10 on volume of 1.37 million, because investors were not attracted by its dividend and rights issue plans, analysts said.
The company's board of directors has proposed a 1.31-for-10 bonus issue to B share holders and a 3.5-for-10 bonus issue to A share holders, a company statement said.

The company said it would also discuss at a meeting of shareholders a plan to make a three-for-10 rights issue, tentatively priced at between 4.5 and 6 yuan, for holders of its A and B shares in 1997.
"The price seems too high considering its B shares are traded at only about HK$6," a trader with a Western bank said.
Livzon Pharmaceutical was the worst performer, losing HK$0.20 or 3.47 percent to end the day at HK$5.56, on volume of 312,900 shares.
The A share index gained 4.29 points or 0.97 percent to 445.15 points. Turnover was 13.8 billion yuan.
